1	\section{Discussion}
2	\label{sec:discussion}
3	
4	\paragraph{A descriptive two-pathway framework.}
5	The results suggest two independent signal pathways and a dilution mechanism that together explain why complete traces degrade SFT learning.
6	
7	\paragraph{Explicit pathway: diagnostic tokens.}
8	The diagnostic token ratio $d$ (\S2.1) correlates with accuracy at $r{=}0.949$ ($p{=}0.014$, df=3; treat as descriptive) across five conditions, and all four models achieve ${\geq}$99.33\% under \texttt{exception\_only} with zero variance on Qwen ($\sigma{=}$0.00, 3 seeds).
9	\texttt{ae\_only}, a strict superset, slightly underperforms \texttt{exception\_only} (Table~\ref{tab:ablation}), indicating that additional content introduces noise even within exception events.
10	
11	\paragraph{Implicit pathway: terminal execution state.}
12	Tail-truncated traces achieve 93--97\% accuracy (Table~\ref{tab:tail_cross_model}) despite $d {\approx} 0$.
13	Tail truncation at ${\geq}$512 tokens captures \texttt{[Line~X]} variable values at final execution steps; terminal variable state implicitly encodes verdict direction because correct values signal passed assertions while error-state variables signal raised exceptions.
14	Below 384 tokens, the globals module dump consumes the entire budget, yielding ${\sim}$73\% ($\approx$ \texttt{no\_trace}).
15	
16	\paragraph{Diagnostic signal dilution in complete traces.}
17	Both pathways' signals exist in full traces but are buried under thousands of intermediate tokens.
18	Controlled gradient masking (\S\ref{sec:density}) attributes ${\leq}$4\% of the gap to gradient dilution, assigning the majority to content quality at inference: diagnostic tokens are too sparse for the model to reliably extract from verbose input.
19	Training dynamics (Appendix~\ref{sec:training_dynamics}) corroborate this: \texttt{exception\_only} converges within 50 steps while \texttt{full\_trace} oscillates without convergence.
20	
21	\paragraph{Why SFT over regex?}
22	The contribution is the diagnostic decomposition, not a prediction system; nonetheless, SFT dominates regex on every axis beyond raw accuracy.
23	SFT retains 97.65\% under marker removal while the regex collapses to 28.49\% (\S\ref{sec:nomarker}), provides 63$\times$ better calibration (\S\ref{sec:calibration}), and transfers bidirectionally across datasets with negligible loss.
24	
25	\paragraph{Design implications.}
26	Complete traces capture only 4--9pp of the ${\sim}$27pp headroom over source code alone, while exception events capture 24--27pp.
27	This runs counter to the field's operating assumption that more trace information should help \citep{chen2025tracepile,wang2025dcsh}; the magnitude and component decomposition are not predictable from information-theoretic priors alone.
28	The two-tier hierarchy suggests a practical fallback: extract exception events first; resort to tail-truncated state otherwise.
29	Tier~2 benefit is model-dependent (Qwen +10.9pp; CodeLlama +0.9pp), so trace design should match deployment model capacity.

\section{Conclusion}

Across four code-specialized models (1.5B--13B, three families), compact exception events (${\geq}$99.33\%) outperform complete traces (77--82\%) by 18--23pp.

That a 7B SFT model surpasses GPT-4o by 12pp under compact input suggests that, within the ${\leq}$13B code-specialized models studied, input curation matters more than model scaling for this task; whether this holds at 30B+ or for general-purpose LLMs remains open.

\section{Introduction}

Execution traces (line-by-line records of a program's runtime behavior) have emerged as a promising input modality for code language models \citep{liu2023codeexecution,chen2025tracepile,ding2024traced,ding2024semcoder,wang2025dcsh,ni2024next}.
The intuition is straightforward: more execution information should help the model make better predictions.
Yet for verdict prediction (classifying whether a test passes or fails), this intuition is wrong.
Complete traces \emph{actively degrade} accuracy compared to compact exception events, despite containing strictly more information.

\begin{figure*}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{fig1_trace_overview}
\vspace{-8pt}
\caption{Overview of the verdict prediction pipeline. Source code and a test input are executed to produce a full raw trace, from which four conditions extract different representations: \texttt{no\_trace} (source code only), \texttt{full\_trace} (complete line-by-line trace), VOTA (Verdict-Optimized Trace Abstraction: exception events, assertion comparisons, and loop summaries), and \texttt{exception\_only} (only exception/error events). Information density decreases from \texttt{full\_trace} to \texttt{exception\_only}, yet accuracy follows the opposite direction (Table~\ref{tab:cross_model}). Appendix~\ref{sec:vota_examples} provides input/output examples.}
\label{fig:trace_overview}
\end{figure*}


Prior work found trace utility to be task-dependent \citep{wang2025dcsh}, but focused on generation-oriented tasks where output noise confounds the analysis.
Verdict prediction offers a cleaner testbed: as binary classification, it isolates the learning signal from generation noise, and controlled component ablation directly measures how trace content affects SFT learning.
This approach aligns with recent *ACL precedent: CRUXEval \citep{gu2024cruxeval} uses execution prediction to probe code reasoning, and NExT \citep{ni2024next} uses trace-augmented chain-of-thought for program repair.

We present a systematic component ablation of trace representations for verdict prediction.
Using 591 problems from HumanEval \citep{chen2021evaluating} and Mostly Basic Python Problems--sanitized (MBPP-sanitized) \citep{austin2021program}, we evaluate four models across three architecture families and 1.5B to 13B parameters: Qwen-2.5-Coder-7B/1.5B-Instruct \citep{qwen2024coder}, CodeLlama-13B-Instruct \citep{roziere2024code}, and DeepSeek-Coder-6.7B-Instruct \citep{deepseek2024coder}.

The central result: complete traces (77--82\%) barely improve over source code alone, while compact exception events achieve near-perfect accuracy (${\geq}$99\%) across all four models, an 18--23 percentage-point (pp) gap (\S\ref{sec:cross_model}).
A simple regex exploiting a format marker matches this ceiling, so the interesting question is not why exceptions help but \emph{why complete traces hurt}.
Marker removal collapses the regex to near-chance while SFT retains $>$97\%; cross-dataset transfer confirms SFT acquires diagnostic patterns beyond format matching (\S\ref{sec:nomarker}).

Gradient masking attributes ${\leq}$4\% of the degradation to gradient dilution; content quality at inference accounts for the majority (\S\ref{sec:density}).
Training dynamics corroborate this: \texttt{exception\_only} converges within 50 steps while \texttt{full\_trace} oscillates without convergence (Appendix~\ref{sec:training_dynamics}).
A tail-truncation budget sweep reveals a sharp performance transition near 512 tokens, coinciding with the first appearance of structured execution markers (\S\ref{sec:trace_length}).

While exception events structurally encode verdict direction (exception present typically implies failure), the non-trivial finding is that providing strictly more information (complete traces containing all exception data) degrades performance by 18--23pp.
Our contributions:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Complete traces degrade SFT verdict accuracy} despite containing all diagnostic information: across four models (1.5B--13B, three families), complete traces (77--82\%) remain near source-code-only levels while compact exception events close an 18--23pp gap to ${\geq}$99.33\% (\S\ref{sec:cross_model}).

\item \textbf{Semantic vs.\ format-marker decomposition}: marker removal collapses a format-exploiting regex by 71pp while SFT drops only 2pp; cross-dataset transfer (99.4--100\%) shows the learned signal generalizes beyond format markers (\S\ref{sec:nomarker}).

\item \textbf{A two-tier signal hierarchy and its mechanistic explanation}: exception/assertion signals (${\geq}$98.53\%) dominate loop compression (77--86\%) by 12+pp with non-overlapping CIs, and a sharp transition at ${\sim}$512 tail tokens yields a practical fallback (\S\ref{sec:ablation}, \S\ref{sec:trace_length}). Controlled gradient masking attributes ${\leq}$4\% of the degradation to gradient dilution, assigning the majority to content quality at inference (\S\ref{sec:density}).
\end{enumerate}
